correctness.rationale: For q=rho/h in (0,1), the beta–Gaussian law gives the central-curvature equation H(q,z)=2z E[T]-1=0 at z=1/(2 delta). The stated Kummer ODE gives a strictly negative second derivative of G at every stationary point; small-z and differentiated large-z signs establish existence and uniqueness. Using G'/G=-H/(2z) there gives z H_z=1-q, so the boxed denominator is exactly 1-q. The q derivative is 2z Cov(T,log(1-T)), strictly negative for the nondegenerate tilted law. Implicit differentiation and delta=1/(2z) give the boxed quotient. At fixed interior q, the quartic derivative at criticality is strictly negative; heat flow converts it to twice the derivative of curvature in thermal variance. The expansion of p'(y)/y in delta-delta_c and y² then yields y²=3(delta_c-delta)+O((delta_c-delta)^2) and a local maximum on the positive side, identified as the off-center mode by the two-mode classification. This is in normalized coordinates and is not uniform in q. The supplied quadrature code was inspected, not run; no floating point check is needed for the analytic assertions.

evidence: From F_a=-I_a H and the exact crossing identity, H_z=(1-q)/z_c. Differentiating the tilted integral gives H_q=2z_c Cov(T,log(1-T)), so differentiating delta_c=1/(2z_c) gives Cov/(1-q). At the root z_c H_z=1-2z_c² Var(T), giving exactly the frozen expression.

The comparison proof itself states the heat equation and p''''(0)<0 at equality. Taylor expansion and evenness give p'(y)/y=p''''(0)[(delta-delta_c)/2+y²/6]+higher orders. Its global result identifies the resulting positive local maximum as the only positive mode.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both remaining formulas are direct corollaries of the comparison source's explicit results in the identical model. No further model-specific bound, uniqueness theorem, or nondegeneracy estimate is needed.
